instruction: Place an order for my work address as per my Amazon shopping list in SimpleNote. For each item in it, buy me the highest rated product available now. If two products have the same rating, pick the cheaper one.
notes: The shopping-list note content is only known at runtime, so the problem instantiates a representative list of two items (list-item-1, list-item-2); add one list-item/query/product triple and one more count object (and bump list-size) per additional item. Items become searchable only after the note is read (note-read); each search discovers the best product (highest rating, cheapest on tie, in stock) for one item via the static best-product fact. Because STRIPS has no quantified/conditional effects, the cart is tracked with a discrete counter (cart-count/count-succ/list-size): place-order is only enabled when exactly list-size distinct best products have been added, and cart-locked forbids adding after ordering, so the order necessarily contains exactly the listed products with quantity 1. amazon.clear_cart is called first so pre-existing cart entries are not ordered (CartEntry changes are ignored by the evaluation). The address id comes from amazon.show_addresses (name == Work) and no address is modified; the payment card id from amazon.show_payment_cards. supervisor.complete_task takes the order and address only as task-record parameters (no API arguments, no answer) and is forced to be last by requiring the goal facts plus (not (task-completed)) everywhere else.
